steps.text: Melt butter in a medium, nonstick saucepan over medium heat. Add cream cheese and garlic powder, whisking until smooth. Add milk, a little at a time, whisking until smooth. Stir in Parmesan cheese and pepper.
Remove from the heat when sauce reaches desired consistency; sauce thickens rapidly. Thin with milk if cooked too long.
Toss with hot pasta to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick and Easy Alfredo Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This easy Alfredo sauce is made with butter, milk, Parmesan, and soft cream cheese to speed up the process with the same rich and creamy results.

video.description: Fettuccine Alfredo is a crowd-pleasing dish that even picky eaters will enjoy. This video shows you how to make Alfredo sauce with a secret ingredient that both speeds up the cooking process and makes it extra indulgent: cream cheese. Just toss the creamy sauce with pasta–and maybe some chicken or shrimp–for a quick and easy dinner in just 10 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I read alot of reviews on this and just kinda figured either I would really like it or really hate it. Here's what I did based on other reviews: used 1 tsp minced garlic with the butter, only used about 1 1/3 cups milk and 4 oz. of parmesean (half a container of kraft grated), about 1/4 tsp black pepper and a few grinds of sea salt. This was the best alfredo I have ever had!!! I didn't even taste a hint of cream cheese and the sauce turned out smooth and creamy and cheesy!! I served it with cut up grilled chicken and fettucine. I LOVED it and so did my boyfriend!! I had some extra sauce so I took it to my friend and she thought it was super delicious!! This will be the only alfredo I make from now on! I hate the jar stuff! The best advice I can give is to have some patience and the whisk IS A MUST!! Put the milk in a little at a time and just keep stirring. Don't use too high of heat and I'm telling you your sauce will turn out perfect!! Thank you for such a great recipe!

I used light cream cheese and skim milk and it was still excellent. The recipe states that this makes 4 servings, but I would say that it easily doubled that. Assuming the 4 servings, using these substitutions drops the calories per serving by 85 and drops the fat by 11.8 grams. The cholesterol drops by 39 mg. (Well worth doing as it is still excellent.)

This really is a great tasting sauce!! I was surprised that you can not taste the cream cheese at all; very "authentic" texture & flavor!! (I was a bit worried at first when my butter and cream cheese did not blend smoothly, and I thought it was because I used margarine and lite cream cheese, but upon adding the first bit of milk it became creamy and the end result was wonderful.) This is an instant classic at my house.

Very excellent recipe. So much smoother, creamier, and easier than other alfredo recipes I've tried. I did make a few of my own adjustments; I used 1 cup of cream and 1 cup of milk like a few others suggested, I used nutmeg instead of garlic powder and pepper, and used parmesean and romano cheeses. It was so luxurious, and reheats slightly better than some homemade sauces. Great for tossing with pasta or more substantial items like meat and veggies. Definately a keeper!

This was ok just going by the recipe. Asked my husband to taste test it, he said tasted more like milk gravy. So I added nutmeg, black pepper, and Italian seasoning. I will admit it is quick, but not really any quicker than making it from a homemade roux.

This recipe is very simple and absolutely delicious! Just some words of wisdom: the sauce thickens as it COOLS not as it gets heated. Please take notice to this as it will save you A LOT of time. If you are heating up your sauce in hopes that it will finally thicken, STOP. Its not going to happen. So turn off the stove, and give yourself a pat on the back; your sauce is perfect, you've done well.
Best ever, no-fail Alfredo sauce. Made as stated, except used minced garlic instead of powder. Been using it for years and love it!!
This is delicious. I made it with whipped garlic and herb cream cheese and being from New Mexico I added Green Chile! Sublime

This turned out great. I had the fresh ingredient to substitute, so I did - I used (3) cloves fresh garlic, grated hard Parmesan, and heavy cream for half the milk called for. I added about a cup of halved cherry tomatoes with the butter, and fresh basil toward the end. This time, I served with grilled chicken breast, but grilled shrimp is even better.

I felt like this turned out well, but I also made various modifications to suit my taste. I made shrimp alfredo, so I usually season my shrimp before I cook it and I make the already sauce in the same pan I added minced garlic and culantro and cooked them in the butter, used Philadelphia cream cheese, and only 1 1/2 cups of the milk (I’ll use all of it next time) and 3/4 of the butter. After I added the milk I let the sauce cook slowly on low and stirred it with my whisk often - it thickened up too well. Still grated theParmesan cheese and added black pepper and garlic powder, and added parsley. Alfredo can be as complicated or simple as you want. The recipe is written to be quick and easy and does what it sets out to do. I don’t typically like what they serve at restaurants because to me it has no flavor. This was a great BASE recipe for me - most recipes you make you’re going to want to doctor in some way.

I must admit that I was skeptical about a cream cheese based Alfredo sauce, but I gave it a try since I had all the ingredients on hand. Well, I'm so glad to have made the recipe! It was remarkably good; my family found it luscious and delicious. It was very easy and quick to put together; my small deviations from the original recipe was to use freshly sautéed garlic (no qualms with using garlic powder - just prefer fresh if I have it) and added some leftover rotisserie chicken. The leftover sauce warmed up nicely - was a little thicker, so added a small bit of milk to loosen it up to its original consistency. It has officially earned on spot in our dinner rotation.
Adequate sauce but a little bland. Very easy though. Will add either real bacon bits or salt next time. It also doesn't thicken as it should. So, either less milk or more cheese next time.

This recipe is the best alfredo sauce I've ever had. That being said I only gave 4 stars because I've made it now several times and it doesn't thicken according to recipe guidelines. You need either less milk or more cheese to get it to thicken and it makes way more then the stated 4 servings. I've yet to try to half the recipe but next time I'm going to.
Great sauce I put raw shrimp and let them cook in the heat of the sauce Great flavor and filling

This has been the best alfredo recipe I've been able to find. I've been making it for literal years and it's a slam dunk every time. I do make one minor adjustment and that is more parmesan cheese. I use 8 ounces instead of 6 because I like it a bit on the thicker side. I also grill up some chicken and have chicken alfredo. I've also added peas or spinach for a splash of color. You can add whatever you want to this recipe as long as you follow the base for the alfredo. Many people get turned away when they see, "cream cheese". I turn away if I don't see cream cheese in an alfredo sauce BECAUSE of this one. This is so much better than any store bought crap you're going to get. Again, 10/10.
It was easier to make than I expected!!!! No more pre-made jar sauces
I've been using this recipe for a few years now. I used minced garlic instead of the powdered garlic for better taste. Anyone I have made this sauce for absolutely loves it.
His was fantastic! I used chicken broth instead Of milk and it was still wonderful.
I just went by taste with the seasoning and it turned out fantastic pretty similar to olive garden taste. Very simple and actually took only like 3 minutes
Delicious but had a wait awhile for sauce to thicken. Ended up adding a small amount of cornstarch. I added a very small amount of red pepper flakes also.
